text: Murgen Hammerfall was the first to use Thunder Clap. In this way he decimated a swathe of invading gnolls in the Alterac Mountains.

Murkblood Overseers are Broken found on Netherwing Ledge in Shadowmoon Valley deep in the mines, somewhere near the flayers. His hand is needed for Seeker of Truth and he himself cuts it off and gives it to you to keep up your disguise.
Murkblood Miners are Broken found on Netherwing Ledge in Shadowmoon Valley.

The Murkshallow is a tribe of makrura found in Drowned Sacellum and Moonshrine Sanctum in Blackfathom Deeps.
Murloc Costume is a Feat of Strength for acquiring a Murloc Costume from BlizzCon 2007.
Murdunk is an orc of the Blackrock clan who helps oversee the worg kennel at Alther's Mill in the Redridge Mountains.
Muscle Memory is a passive Mistweaver monk ability, available at level 20.
Munch Windhoof is a tauren flight master located at Dawnchaser Retreat in the Krasarang Wilds.
Murkalot is a feats of strength achievement earned for obtaining Murkalot from BlizzCon 2013.
Murkmorphosis is an ability used by Murkidan during a Pet Battle.
The Mur'gul Clam Shucker appears in Rise of the Naga. It is a slightly more powerful Mur'gul Reaver.
__NOTOC__ Murkloc Cave is a small murloc cave in the Shipwreck Cove of Highmountain. It is the home of the newly formed Murkloc tribe, led by Murky.
Mushroom Vendor is a drogbar fungus vendor located inside Neltharion's Lair, a dungeon in Highmountain. He sells the Ketchum Tablet required to complete the achievement Got to Ketchum All.

Murrgly is a murloc from a fishing village in the Forgotten Coast in Feralas. He used to teach his nephew Murky to fish, but he knew that the youngling wasn't good at it. He, his wife Murr and several other murlocs were captured by the Gordunni clan and brought to Dire Maul to fight for the ogre's amusement. When Aramar Thorne was brought there and had to fight the gnoll Hackle and the wyvern One-Eye, Murrgly showed Thalyss Greyoak a thorn dome containing her three cubs. In the ensuing chaos caused by the Hidden, the murlocs were freed and escaped. Murrgly and Murr were briefly reunited with Murky who saved them from being recaptured by Wordok. Murrgly was now proud of his nephew who decided
Murloc Battlemasters is a feats of strength achievement earned for obtaining Knight-Captain Murky and Legionnaire Murky from BlizzCon 2016.
The Murloc Treasure is located at the Western Spray on Mechagon Island. It is opened with the Chief's Key.
Mushrooms are mushrooms located in the Fleeting Forest on Mechagon Island. The Mushroom with ID 135497 will spawn Fungarian Furor.

The Murkloc are a group of murlocs inhabiting Murkloc Cave in Highmountain. This tribe of murlocs was formed when King Mrgl-Mrgl wanted the Swamprock to become more peaceful. He kidnapped a few of their tadpoles and placed Murky in change of them. After defeating Clawdayshus, they make their base in his cave.
Murloc Soup can be found on Island Expeditions. It heals adventurers to full health.

Murkfathom Reach is an underwater trench located off the coast of Fort Daelin in Stormsong Valley. The remains of shipwrecks can be seen resting on the ocean floor as well as an abundance of sealife scattered throughout the area including eels, turtles, and sharks.
Murderous Tempest is an air elemental located in Island Expeditions.
Murmurs in the Dark is a trinket dropped by Senthii, As Gul'dan at the Star Lake Amphitheater in Ardenweald.
Murmuring Shawl is an anima power obtained from anima caches in Torghast, Tower of the Damned.
The Murloc Hopper is a flying machine found in Azmerloth. It is piloted by Amrrgla Grglllhrrt. Players control the guns during Deathwingurlugull!, part of the Thaldraszus storyline.

Munitions Barrels are located at the Overseer's Redoubt in Tol Dagor. They can be ignited by the shots of Heavy Cannons or the abilities of Ashvane Flamecasters. The explosion will damage everyone in range.

The Murloc Gurgler is a murloc used in the Blizzard Warcraft III 'Monolith'. Because of the power of the Monolith which has been attracting wildlife with its mysterious energies, it allows a Murloc Gurgler to gather gold and build Murloc Fishing Pool. A Murloc Gurgler is the lowest level of Murloc in Warcraft III costing One food and 50 gold and is classified as a worker. A Murloc Gurgler can build Murloc Fishing Pools allowing it to train more of their brethren for combat purposes and Monolith shards, becoming the Murlocs only form of defensive structure. The appearance of Gurglers are much smaller than other murlocs and have a tint of yellow to their skin.
Myizz Luckycatch is a goblin fishing trainer located in Booty Bay in the Cape of Stranglethorn. When the city was attacked by pirates, he was hanging off of a rope.

__NOTOC__ Mux Manascrambler is a goblin located in Gadgetzan in Tanaris. He can be found in a house in the center of the city, behind Driz Plunkbow and his Butcherbots. He was present during the Legion Invasions.
__NOTOC__ Myriam Moonsinger is a night elf located on a hill just south of the huge pig skull-shaped entrance to Razorfen Downs in the Thousand Needles.
Mutilate is a level 12 Assassination rogue ability that requires two daggers, dealing damage and generating combo points.
__NOTOC__ Myrokos Silentform is a blood elf located at Ravenholdt Manor in the Alterac Mountains. He is also found in the Hall of Shadows.

__NOTOC__ Mutated Root Lashers are orchids found in the Ammen Fields on Azuremyst Isle. They have been irradiated by a power crystal which broke away from the Exodar and fell into Silverline Lake. Botanist Taerix analyzed samples from these lashers in order to create a Neutralizing Agent capable of cleansing the lake and returning the nearby Volatile Mutations to their original forms.
The Myrmidon's Cape is a continent drop from level 40 - 50 Eastern Kingdoms mobs.
A reward from the Darkmoon Faire related quest Your Fortune Awaits You.... Whatever could it contain?

Mutated Owlkin are owlkin mobs that can be found in the Nestlewood Hills on Azuremyst Isle. They were once Nestlewood Owlkin but have been irradiated by a power core which fell from the Exodar into the Silverline Lake. They originally had a habit of attacking adventurers on sight, which made them an obstacle during Spare Parts (Azuremyst Isle) and Inoculation.
Mysterious Shells were the second most powerful type of bullets available prior to .
Mysterious Arrows were the second most powerful type of arrows available in , adding 46.5 DPS.
The Musty Tome is located in the city hall of the Ruins of Andorhal, Western Plaguelands.

The Mysterious Red Crystal is located in the Darkshore. Hostile moonkin are being drawn to it. It seems that embedded inside the crystal are a few small fragments of bone, as well as half of a jawbone of what may be a humanoid.
The Mysterious Egg can be found atop a tree in Nagrand. It can be reached by either using Jump-a-tron 4000 or if you can fly, by mount. Later found out they are of Windroc Matriarch.

Mysterious Tarot is an Inscription spell that creates one of three 'Rogue' cards at random: Ace of Rogues, Two of Rogues or Three of Rogues. Combining one of each card creates a Rogues Deck, which begins Darkmoon Faire quest Rogues Deck (quest).
Mutated Morrowgrain is inside the Evergreen Herb Casing when it doesn't contain Morrowgrain. It is essentially useless, and best sold or destroyed immediately.
in Hearthstone.]] Mutated abominations are powerful abomination constructs of the Scourge. They were created by Professor Putricide.

Muzzle is a tamed black bear located in the Hunter Trainer dwellings of the Dwarven District in Stormwind City.

Musu Gentlemoon is a tauren druid trainer at the Crossroads in the Northern Barrens. She defended the town during the Legion Invasions. During the Fourth War, she was encountered by Alliance champions in the Wailing Caverns.
The Mysterious Grimoire rarely drops from specific level-appropriate dungeon bosses with the Darkmoon Adventurer's Guide in their bags.
Myrla Stoneround is a barmaid in the Golden Keg, the inn located in the Dwarven District of the human capital of Stormwind City.

Mysterious Den is the easternmost of the three caves in the Red Stone Run. Immediately to the north is Kukuru's Grotto, and further west is Tsavo'ka's Den. The cave is blocked by a cave-in. However, at the base of the cave in is a Tattered Note... The tattered note suggests to find one of the Timeless Legends on the isle, and use the provided bonus ability on the Cave-In. Should players somehow find themselves locked inside the mysterious den, there is a Rock-breaking Hammer on the inside that can be used to break the cave-in as well. Either method of breaking the cave-in will immediately summon Spelurk, a rare mistlurker.
Mutant Horrors are fleshbeasts found in Shadowmoon Valley. They were mutated by fel energy.

.]] Myrmidons are naga units. They use scimitars and tridents as their weapons. They first appeared after the Third War, accompanying Lady Vashj and Illidan Stormrage. On the Broken Shore a myrmidon ensnared Tyrande Whisperwind. With the arrival of Malfurion Stormrage and Maiev Shadowsong, Illidan had to depart and the myrmidon covered his escape. In Lordaeron, myrmidons were sent to scout rivers for missing Tyrande. A group of them attacked the ship Wavecutter from Theramore on which Lo'Gosh and his companions were. Another group attacked Feathermoon Stronghold after the Cataclysm. They also became troops of the Illidari stationed at the Fel Hammer.

The designer wishes us luck as the requirement to get this roll is "simultaneously no where near as mean [as The Immortal (achievement)], and significantly meaner".

Myskia is a massive stoneborn goliath located in Revendreth. Since he typically appears alongside the Stone Legion Generals, General Kaal and General Grashaal, he is likely a high-ranking stoneborn. Myskia initially appears during The Master Awaits when Kaal asks him to fly the Maw Walker to the Grand Palisade. Once The Accuser is captured, Denathrius entrusts Myskia with transporting her cage to The Fearstalker for humbling. Finally, once the player joins Prince Renathal's rebellion, Myskia is battled and killed during The Master of Lies.

Mushy Snowplum is looted from Lady Moonberry's Disgruntled Gift in the Ember Court.

The n'raqi, commonly known as the faceless ones or the faceless, are a monstrous race that arose from the organic matter that seeped from the Old Gods' blighted forms during the primordial era of Azeroth. Cunning and intelligent, they serve their eldritch masters with fanatical loyalty and are known to be virtually unstoppable juggernauts. During times of war, the n'raqi serve as the commanders and taskmasters of the Old Gods' forces, turning the insane worshipers and chaotic forces into a capable military force. The faceless ones were first seen serving a forgotten one in the depths of Azjol-Nerub during the events of Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne. They made their first appearance in Worl

An NPC (Non-Player Character) is any character you encounter and interact with in World of Warcraft that is not controlled by other human players — they are generated and controlled by the game server. NPCs are either Neutral or affiliated with a particular faction ( Alliance or Horde). You cannot attack NPCs of your faction and you must be "at war" (set in Reputation tab of your character sheet) with a neutral NPC's faction to attack them. Typical examples of NPCs include flight masters, innkeepers, quest givers, vendors, trainers, and guards. or NPCs may have a bag (, if a vendor) or talk bubble (, if you can talk to them) cursor when you mouse-over them. The serpentine naga (sometimes pluralized as nagas) are some of the most formidable villains of Azeroth. Masters of sorcery, the naga were formerly Highborne night elves, members of Queen Azshara's court during the age of the Kaldorei Empire. Following the War of the Ancients, and the Great Sundering caused by the destruction of the Well of Eternity, they were transformed into naga by the Old God N'Zoth after Azshara pledged herself to his cause, dedicating her people to become his army and recreate the Black Empire on Azeroth. An NPC class is a class held by a non player character. Most characters are not heroes. They do not spend their days battling monsters, searching for magic items, or blasting their enemies with spells; they plow farms, make shoes, and sell rope. Some are artisans, some are grand or petty nobles; but whatever the case, they do not possess heroic classes like arcanist or warrior. Instead, they have other classes. Some characters, particularly those who oppose or ally with heroes, are suitably villainous or heroic to warrant the use of the base classes. These are the classes for those who do not spend a lot of time adventuring.

The naga explorers are an expedition of naga explorers found at Nek'mani Wellspring in Cape of Stranglethorn. They have advanced upon the Nek'mani Wellspring, a Holy Spring high above the bluffs, subject of great conflict amongst religious and mystical scholars, every race in Azeroth claiming that the spring waters were made divine for their people. Some of them carry stalks of some kind of valuable ocean reed they call akiris reed.

A mystical Hero, adept at ranged combat. These scaly denizens of the ocean have often been associated with the coming of prodigious storms, but few have actually seen them rise from the sea and lived to tell the tale. Attacks land and air units.

Nambu are large carnivorous plants that exist on the Darkspear islands, possibly only within First Home. They have furry lips which cover fibrous teeth around their gaping maw. Nambu have lightning reflexes and are capable of funneling poison into their prey. While their jaws are strong and able to lock down one many creatures, pulling them from the ground will put an end to their fight.

Naga brutes (also known as behemoths and hulks) are huge, mutated naga used as heavy fighters and even as siege weapons by the naga army. Some have rank, while some act more like mere beasts. No explanation for their origins have been given. It is known that naga brutes have the ability to speak, such as many Sashj'tar naga brutes in Azuregale Bay in Suramar. One, in particular, is Har'kess the Insatiable. Archmage Khadgar, aside from calling them "brutes", also referred to them as "bruisers".

Naanu was one of the three final Sporemounds faced by Grond, the other two being Zang and Botaan. It wore a fleece of dense jungles. After Zang was torn apart by Grond, the giant pressed his attack against Naanu and crushed it between his unyielding hands. The lifeless Sporemound collapsed to the ground. Its broken husk would slowly sink into the earth and become a region called Tanaan Jungle. Naigtal is a nighttime world of giant mushrooms, resembling Zangarmarsh on Outland. It is one of the Invasion Points of the Burning Legion, accessible from Argus. The planet is (or at one point was) home to at least one intelligent race. Sergeant Krashj hails from Naigtal and used to train herds of Marsh Shamblers for pit combat during every "Soltian festival".

The near-humans (also simply known as the humans) of Draenor were an in-universe speculative race used by Garona and Medivh to interpret the former's non-orcish heritage. This concept dates from after the retcon that the orcs spent more than ten years in Azeroth after the opening of the Dark Portal until the launching the First War, and from before the Lost Ones were retconed as being mutated draenei. As such, the existence of a near-human race on Draenor was required in order to keep Garona's background coherent. The final, canon story is that before Garona's heritage as a half-orc/half-draenei was revealed, Gul'dan deceived her into believing that she was half-human.

Despite the frustrated cries of players personally affected by a nerf, such things are usually necessary to protect the integrity of the game balance as a whole. Nerubian Slavemaker is an epic crossbow. It was the most powerful ranged weapon prior to release.

The nether ray is a beast native to /Outland and Bonich. It has a body much like a stingray's (thus the name) with a long tail and two feathery plumes. It has crystalline growths and stripes running down its body, and all types are brightly colored. Nether rays have been found in Netherstorm, Zangarmarsh, and Shadowmoon Valley and are tamable as hunter pets. Nether Rays are among the most trusted, versatile mounts in all of Outland and beyond.

Nestlewood Thicket is an area in southern Ammen Vale, filled with owlkin. It is located within the draenei starting zone and most draenei should reach this area around level 3-4. The owlkin have gathered the scattered Emitter Spare Parts here and in the Nestlewood Hills (see Spare Parts (Azuremyst Isle)). Unfortunately, some of the native owlkin have been mutated by the radiation from the power crystals that fell from the draenei ship the Exodar, and have become hostile to travelers. Some draenei are attempting to inoculate the unaffected owlkin using an Inoculating Crystal to keep them from being mutated like their fellow friends (see Inoculation).

They're generally peaceful, but after the recent crash of the Exodar, radiation from the ship's broken power crystals has caused some of them to become Mutated Owlkin. The owlkin have also absconded with some of the draenei's s which were scattered about the area. Vindicator Aldar has asked adventurers to inoculate these owlkin using Botanist Taerix's Inoculating Crystal, hoping to protect them from mutating. Unfortunately, their Mutated Owlkin brethren are too far gone to help.
